tagline: Two million visitors a year — and every single one begins and ends the trip on a boat.
summary: Boracay has no airport and no bridge: all 2.1M+ annual visitors funnel through the Caticlan jetty ↔ Cagban crossing, making it one of the world's densest short-hop boat corridors. After the landmark 2018 six-month environmental closure, the island reopened under a strict clean-water, capacity-managed regime — a standing mandate that a quiet, zero-emission, wake-free foiling fleet answers directly, while the Carabao and Romblon island arc (5–53 nm) sits untapped just beyond the gateway.

use_cases.title: Electric gateway shuttle: Caticlan ↔ Cagban
use_cases.body: The whole island boards through one ~2 nm crossing. A scheduled all-electric foiling shuttle (Pioneer II now; the 12–15-pax N35 Shuttle as the native scheduled-arrivals platform from 2027) replaces diesel pumpboats on the single highest-frequency corridor in the Philippines — silent, wake-free, and on-message for the post-2018 environmental regime.

use_cases.title: Beyond-Boracay day loops
use_cases.body: Carabao Island (~5 nm), Crocodile Island and the Tablas coast (~21 nm) become smooth 10–40-minute foiling hops instead of weather-dependent open-banca rides — unlocking the next ring of destinations without adding wake or noise to a recovering shoreline.

use_cases.title: Resort-jetty premium transfers
use_cases.body: Direct foiling arrivals to Shangri-La Boracay, Discovery Shores, Henann Palm Beach and the Newcoast marina frontage — turning the jetty-queue-plus-trike arrival into one seamless premium hop from Caticlan.

use_cases.title: Romblon arc connectivity
use_cases.body: San Agustin and Romblon harbor (~41 nm), Sibuyan (~49 nm) and Corcuera (~53 nm) are all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — a clean inter-island feeder network for communities relying on infrequent pumpboat and RORO sailings today.

use_cases.title: Manila gateway line-haul
use_cases.body: Manila ↔ Boracay (~210 nm) as a premium-experiential Quanta-LR line-haul from H2 2026+ — hybrid range with no charging-infrastructure dependency at the leisure end.

journeys.today: Diesel pumpboat shuttle with queues at both piers; the crossing every one of 2.1M+ annual visitors must make, in both directions.
journeys.with_navier: A silent, zero-emission foiling shuttle gliding over the strait — no fumes at the pier, no wake on a shoreline that was closed for six months to recover.

journeys.today: Open banca, ~45 min and swell-exposed; trips drop off whenever the wind picks up.
journeys.with_navier: A ~15-minute foiling hop above the chop — Carabao becomes a reliable everyday extension of a Boracay stay.

journeys.today: Infrequent pumpboat and RORO sailings; a half-day commitment that keeps the arc off most itineraries.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth ~75-minute all-electric run at 20 kt cruise — the marble-and-waterfall islands of Romblon open up as day trips.

journeys.with_navier: A single Quanta-LR coastal line-haul (~210 nm) door-to-island — the premium-experiential alternative arriving H2 2026+.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Tailor-made geometry: the ~2 nm Caticlan↔Cagban gateway, ~5 nm Carabao hop and the whole Tablas–Romblon–Sibuyan arc (21–53 nm) sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with rotation margin — a dense gateway shuttle plus an island-arc feeder network from one charging base at Caticlan.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Manila ↔ Boracay (~210 nm) and Cebu ↔ Boracay gateway line-hauls from H2 2026+, hybrid with no charging-infrastructure dependency at the destination — connecting the island to the national mesh beyond the 70 nm electric ring.

competitive_landscape: The water is run today by the slot-allocated diesel pumpboat fleet on the Caticlan↔Cagban crossing, banca cooperatives for island-hopping, and RORO/fastcraft operators (Montenegro Shipping, Starlite) on the Batangas–Caticlan and Romblon runs. Volume is enormous and proven — 2M+ boat-borne arrivals a year — but the experience is unchanged in decades: queues, fumes, spray and weather cancellations. That installed demand on a capacity-managed, environmentally supervised corridor is precisely the modernization opportunity.
seasonality: Amihan (Nov–Feb) brings the calm, dry peak season on the west-facing White Beach side; habagat (Jun–Sep) flips swell onto the west coast and shifts operations to the Bulabog (east) side — a seasonal side-flip foiling handles gracefully by riding above the chop. The Jun–Nov typhoon season imposes statutory PAGASA signal closures (Signal 3+ halts all marine traffic); within the open windows, foiling smoothness materially raises usable, comfortable operating days.
regulatory_note: Post-2018, Boracay operates under the Boracay Inter-Agency Task Force and DENR oversight with visitor caps and strict wastewater/coastal rules — the strongest standing clean-operations mandate of any Philippine destination, and the island already converted land transport to e-trikes. A zero-emission, wake-free marine fleet is the water-side completion of that policy. Vessel certification through MARINA; jetty access via the slot-allocated Caticlan public pier (LGU/Philippine Ports Authority).

precedents.where: Maldives (with JIH Global), first 5 vessels in 2026, 3-year phased rollout
precedents.why_it_matters: The playbook for archipelago-scale clean marine mobility — Boracay's gateway-plus-arc geometry is a natural replication site.
The island has already chosen electric-first on land; the boat fleet is the unfinished half of the same policy.
